# SightPress

> SightPress is an accessible, open-source content management system (CMS) for everyone, designed with blind and low-vision content creators and audiences who use assistive technology in mind. It is written in modern, object-oriented PHP and licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Status: pre-launch. Test release 0.4.0 (24 November 2026) is available for developers and testers; version 1.0 will be the first for live websites.

Key facts:

- Mission: accessibility is the floor, quality design is the goal, and neither is ever traded for the other. Accessibility is a release requirement and cannot be switched off.
- Standards: the admin, sign-in pages, default theme and emails target WCAG 2.2 AA; SightPress as an authoring tool targets ATAG 2.0 AA. Conformance reports (WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549, ATAG 2.0) are planned from version 1.0.
- Releases so far: 0.4.0 (24 November 2026): Themes you can choose per site, captions and transcripts, large and resumable uploads, and optional cloud storage; 0.3.0 (19 November 2026): Private analytics with charts you can read in words and tables, and an optional AI assistant that only suggests; 0.2.0 (19 November 2026): Languages and translations, site search, members-only pages, older versions, scheduling and redirects; 0.1.0 (17 November 2026): The first usable version: build pages from blocks, publish checks, the admin panel and several sites in one installation.
- Works today (0.4.0): pages built from ten block types; checks before publishing (image descriptions, link text, captions, transcripts, heading order) that stop a page with an accessibility error; several sites and languages in one installation; translations, hreflang and a sitemap per language; site search; members-only pages and self-registration; six-digit codes instead of email links; older versions compared word by word, scheduling and redirects; private cookieless analytics with chart summaries in words and data tables; themes per site with colour contrast checks; captions and transcripts; large, resumable uploads; optional cloud storage with a CDN; a Markdown version of every public page.
- Optional AI assistant, off for new sites: uses the organisation's own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, or a compatible or self-hosted service); it only suggests, never publishes, and AI-written alt text and translations must be checked by a person before publishing.
- Runs with Docker on MariaDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQLite, with FrankenPHP, nginx or Apache, and local or cloud storage. Loads no third-party scripts or fonts.
- In progress (0.5.0): Add-on modules from other developers, custom roles, email and domain rules, and optional text messages.
- Before 1.0: security review, UK/EU privacy tools (download or delete your data, retention, generated privacy policy), performance, guides for running on a public server, full documentation and an independent accessibility review.
- After 1.0 (plans that may change): a link checker, PDF checks, readability scores, visitor display preferences without an overlay, an accessible form builder and media player, a WordPress importer, and official modules for news, events, documents, newsletters, donations, meetings, consultations, bookings, podcasts and more.
- Built for blind and low-vision creators; charities, NGOs, councils and public bodies that must meet WCAG 2.2 AA and EN 301 549; small businesses; individuals; and audiences who rely on assistive technology.
- Founder and lead developer: Pedro Ferreira, a Portuguese web developer based in London who became blind in 2024.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sightpress.org/): what SightPress is, where it stands, how to get involved, FAQ and contact
- [About](https://sightpress.org/about/): mission, who it is for, how it is built and tested, the creator and the community
- [Features](https://sightpress.org/features/): what works in 0.4.0, what is in progress, and the plans before and after 1.0
- [Articles](https://sightpress.org/articles/): articles by Pedro Ferreira, with an Atom feed at https://sightpress.org/articles/feed.xml
- [Documentation](https://docs.sightpress.org/): getting started, how-to guides and reference
